newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Mediaeval skeletons dug up in Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Mediaeval skeletons dug up in Ireland.

text.p: Thirty-five skeletons dating back 700 years have been uncovered during excavation work in Ireland, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The skeletons, believed to be the remains of mediaeval friars, were unearthed as construction workers prepared the foundations for a shopping complex in the town of Mullingar, the Irish Times .

A religious relic believed to have originated at the shrine of Santiago de Compostela in Spain, fragments of 13th and 14th century glazed French pottery and parts of what appeared to be a bronze clasp, were also found.
Archaeologists said the skeletons were well preserved because of the free-draining gravel in which they were buried.
